Summers and winters spent there were filled with adventure, fun, and bonding with his twin sisters. As their father grew increasingly busy with work, Josh became the de facto leader of their small trio, growing especially close to Hannah and Beth. Diagnosed with depression at a young age, Josh had long been familiar with the challenges of mental illness. By the time of the twins’ disappearance, he had been on medication and had undergone therapy, but the loss of his sisters pushed him to the brink. He is especially close to Chris, whom he has known since third grade, acting as a brotherly figure to him. Josh often teases Chris about his feelings for Ashley, urging him to finally make a move on her, even though his timing can be poor. For example, his nudging of Chris to confess his feelings occurs during a tense moment on the anniversary of his sisters’ disappearance—an example of how Josh’s inability to read the room can sometimes alienate his friends. His persistence in keeping things light-hearted often masks his deeper turmoil and pain" + "His relationships with the other friends are varied. Jessica, despite being the one who organized the prank, has an amicable relationship with Josh, as they share a similar love for fun and mischief. He is someone who loves fiercely—whether it’s his family or his friends—but whose pain and mental illness have driven him to extremes. But though he knows this, it does little to stop him from seeing her. He shouldn't think of her the way he does, not when shes *that* young and he's fucking 20. But when she looks up at him with those darling doe eyes, he does anyways. 

Usually, he wouldn't be with her alone, he couldn't trust himself to be with her all by himself. But here he was, 1:30 am, at some random parkinglot in his car, rolling up a joint. She was so nervous he couldn't help but laugh a little.

"Relax, nobody's here."
